Reading (locked before any Lean is shown) — def LevyStochCalc.Probability.markedPredictableSigma

Paper notion (eq:fubiniiso): P ⊗ E, the product σ-algebra of the predictable σ-field P on
time × Ω and the mark σ-algebra E — equivalently, the σ-algebra on time × Ω × E generated by
the marked predictable rectangles (s, t] × F × A (F ∈ F_s, A ∈ E), plus {0} × F × A (F ∈ F_0).
Faithful Lean definition: MeasurableSpace.generateFrom (markedPredictableRect) or the
product predictableSigma ⊗ E (these coincide). Edge: time-0 generators as for
predictableSigma; it must be ≤ the ambient product σ-algebra B(time) ⊗ F ⊗ E.

comparison.text:
Comparison — markedPredictableSigma (MarkedPredictable.lean:43-47)

Lean: MeasurableSpace.generateFrom (markedPredictableRect ℱ ν) on Ω × ℝ × E.
Against my reading (P ⊗ E = σ of the marked predictable rectangles, ≤ ambient product):
- Generated by the rectangles, as anticipated; ≤ the ambient product σ-algebra
  (markedPredictableSigma_le, used in the specs).
- Equals the classical P ⊗ E on Ω × (0,∞) × E for σ-finite ν; {s ≤ 0} × Ω × E is an atom
  (no time-0 cell): narrower only at the dt⊗dP⊗ν-null time 0, harmless for the paper's class /
  a.e. uses; time ℝ with negative times lumped into that atom.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices of markedPredictableSigma, and why each is harmless:
1. Generated without time-0 rectangles, so {s ≤ 0} × Ω × E is an atom: differs from the classical
   P ⊗ E only at time 0, a dt⊗dP⊗ν-null set; every classical predictable integrand has an
   a.e.-equal representative measurable for it, and the paper uses predictable integrands only up
   to such null sets.
2. Finite-mass mark sets in the generators: no change for σ-finite ν.
3. Time axis ℝ (negative times absent from the paper, lumped into the time-0 atom).

author_review.disagreements:
The author's review, as shown by rv.py author, consists of the review marker only (no reading text, no item-by-item comparison), so there is no stated position of the author to disagree with on substance.
Not recorded there, and the main point of this unit: the marked predictable σ-algebra has no
time-0 generator, so a MarkedPredictable process is constant on {s ≤ 0} × Ω × E — narrower than
classical P ⊗ E at time 0 (where an F_0 ⊗ E-measurable value is allowed), and inconsistent with
the unmarked predictableSigma, which does have the initial cell. Harmless only because time 0 is
dt⊗dP⊗ν-null and every use is up to such null sets (the specs force U = 0 off [0,T]); the review
should record this.
